title: Integrating drone technology in STEM education: Curriculum, pedagogy and learning outcomes
extended_summary:
This paper examines how a Drone Technology-Enabled STEM Curriculum (DTESC) can support secondary students’ learning across cognitive, psychomotor, and affective domains. The authors frame the work around “dronagogy,” a pedagogical approach that uses drones to create interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary learning experiences. The study asks whether drone-integrated instruction can improve students’ understanding of STEM content, their hands-on technical and design skills, and their attitudes toward STEM learning.

The intervention was implemented with 16 Grade 9–10 students from one secondary school in Hong Kong. Over 10 weeks, students completed a 36-hour program outside regular school hours that included multidisciplinary lessons, interdisciplinary modules, and transdisciplinary project-based tasks such as drone coding, landscape surveying, and designing a drone-assisted water sampling system. Data sources included a knowledge test, rubric-based assessment of design and presentation tasks, reflection journals, and a course evaluation survey.

Results showed strong engagement and satisfaction, with notable gains in psychomotor and affective outcomes. Students performed well in science and social studies-related content and in collaborative engineering and presentation tasks, but mathematics and higher-order technology reasoning were weaker areas. The authors conclude that drone-based STEM curriculum can be effective for engagement and practical skill development, but that future versions should provide stronger scaffolding for mathematical reasoning, abstract conceptualization, and higher-order cognitive learning.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a small-sample mixed-methods pilot study without a control group or pretest-posttest inferential comparison. The evidence is useful and peer-reviewed, but credibility is limited by the absence of experimental contrast and the very small sample (n=16).
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports positive but mostly descriptive outcomes with no effect sizes and no comparison condition. The impact appears promising for a small pilot, but the magnitude and generalizability are unclear.

interventions.use_case: Drone technology-enabled integrated STEM curriculum (DTESC) using drones for interdisciplinary learning activities such as drone-assisted water sampling, autonomous navigation coding, landscape surveying, and entrepreneurial drone proposal design.
ChatGPT 3.5 used to translate students' reflection journal entries from Chinese to English for clarity during qualitative analysis, not as the instructional intervention.

finding.finding_summary: The DTESC improved students' science-domain knowledge and understanding. On the 18-item knowledge test, students scored a mean of 3.00/4 in science (75% correct; SD=0.73) and showed generally satisfactory performance on higher-order science questions, indicating strengthened scientific comprehension in authentic drone-based contexts.
finding.measure: 18-item STEM knowledge test; science domain subscore

finding.finding_summary: Mathematics was the weakest cognitive domain in the DTESC. Students scored a mean of 1.75/3 in mathematics (58% correct; SD=0.68), and the paper reports difficulty applying polygon-angle and trigonometry knowledge to real-world drone tasks. The intervention improved hands-on application overall, but mathematics transfer and higher-order reasoning remained limited.
finding.measure: 18-item STEM knowledge test; mathematics domain subscore

finding.finding_summary: Students showed strong performance in the non-STEM PSHE domain embedded in the curriculum. The PSHE subscore mean was 2.75/3 (92% correct; SD=0.45), suggesting the drone-integrated thematic curriculum successfully conveyed history/geography/social content alongside STEM activities.
finding.measure: 18-item STEM knowledge test; PSHE domain subscore

finding.finding_summary: The curriculum produced strong gains in psychomotor and collaborative competencies. All four student groups successfully completed the engineering design task; the best group achieved 40/40 on the rubric, and proposal presentations were rated as satisfactory to strong on creativity, feasibility, and teamwork. The paper reports no formal effect size, but performance evidence indicates improved hands-on problem solving, design skills, and collaboration.
finding.measure: Rubric scores for drone-assisted water sampling system; rubric/likert ratings for entrepreneurial proposal presentations

finding.finding_summary: Students reported high engagement, enjoyment, motivation, and resilience during DTESC participation. In the course evaluation, 88% strongly supported continuing the program, 81% recognized its cross-disciplinary benefits, and 75% valued the hands-on practice; qualitative journals also highlighted joyful learning, active engagement, and resilience in the face of failure.
finding.measure: Reflection journals and course evaluation survey
